reviewer: Codex delegated eval_review agent; independent of the Aalto and tool draft authors
method: Read complete 11 assigned Aalto content documents and applicable LICENSE, all 47 candidate questions/targets, exact cited spans, production tool schemas/mocks/scorer/policy, and comparison questions. Model content review plus standard-library exact checks. No external sources or inference requests.
review_exposure: Not blind: author sidecars and historical comparison datasets were available. No human review claimed. Reviewer previously authored the 22 final drafts used only for overlap comparison.

checks_run.normalization: Unicode NFKC, casefold, Unicode word tokens
checks_run.semantic_dedup: Model inspection found no duplicate objectives. Lexical scores used only as triage, not a semantic guarantee.

checks_not_run: No new production scorer execution; the author-reported 44 synthetic scorer tests are inherited evidence, not rerun here.
No compilation, shell or Slurm execution, profiling, model inference, student evaluation, real cluster actions or runtime policy verification.
release_caveats: All Aalto items are development-exposed and must retain the exact source revision and Triton site scope; module names, PMIx suggestion, GPU policies and approximate sampling interval are not claims about Leonardo or every Slurm cluster.
References with external example filenames explicitly assume those programs exist and use commands documented inline. Full program behavior and runtime success have not been verified.
dev-aalto-002 cites both the GPU reference and the GPU tutorial within the same reserved family. Preserve both support entries instead of flattening provenance to one path.

dev-aalto-035 cited loop/output spans are supported; the same source also shows equals-form #SBATCH --output at lines 74-77. Its changed output filename is incidental to the new progress/buffering objective.

Tool scoring assesses only first-response decision, arguments and deterministic mock executability. No-call nonempty text can pass without asking a useful question or truthfully explaining a limitation; tool-023 is not a complete hallucination test.

tool-020 is an explicitly authorized isolated mock action. Its CPU-only script on a GPU-like mock partition is accepted by that fixture and must not be promoted as proof of real cluster policy/resource validity.
The normal scripts use source-compatible compositions. No exact-reference wording should be required from models when a supported equivalent answer satisfies the task.
No new source or review resolves the original six seeds’ 18 unknown provenance fields.
Keep all new development and final material, references and paraphrases outside training, gold prompts, feedback and preferences. Final drafts retain construction exposure and are not claimed blind.

tool_items.content_and_novelty_review: Both filters are explicit and supported. The mock intersects state and partition; the visible policy allows this queue query without a job ID. This adds a conjunctive argument requirement beyond the existing PENDING-only query.

tool_items.content_and_novelty_review: stdout must be explicitly selected because stderr is the default. Omitted tail_lines or integer 20 both preserve the requested default; string 20 is not allowed. This is not a tail-number or ID-only variation of tool-002.
tool_items.scope_limit: The selected default fixture has a readable stdout log. No diagnosis, log summarization, or claims about a real job are scored.

tool_items.content_and_novelty_review: partition_info with no filter supplies all configured partitions and requested CPU/memory/time fields, including the CPU-only fixture. gpu_availability has different scope and fields; this differs from one-partition tool-005.

tool_items.content_and_novelty_review: The complete supplied script and explicit mock-submission permission justify submit_job with test_only=false or omitted. This is meaningfully different from tool-009 validation-only permission. Script case/content must remain exact under the current scorer transport rules.
tool_items.scope_limit: Mock submission only. No script execution, allocation, job completion, resource validation, real Slurm submission, or student quality has occurred. Accepted script transport differences follow the existing v2 scorer, not a new scorer.

tool_items.content_and_novelty_review: The API requires full script text and the inventory has no arbitrary file reader. A filename cannot satisfy that argument. No-call clarification is appropriate; inventing a new wrapper script would not submit the supplied but unread content.
tool_items.scope_limit: The no-call label only checks that the first response contains no tool call and is nonempty. It does not validate whether the assistant actually requests the right missing information.

tool_items.content_and_novelty_review: Two explicit IDs do not resolve which is obsolete. The visible clarify-first policy forbids guessing or discovery before clarification for the unresolved action target. This differs from simply missing an ID.
tool_items.scope_limit: Only no-call behavior is scored. The semantic quality of a clarification is unscored, and the fixture states cannot establish the user meaning of obsolete.

tool_items.content_and_novelty_review: None of the eight available tools runs an arbitrary command in the current login shell. Submitting a batch job would change the requested operation. No-call is correct for this inventory.
tool_items.scope_limit: The scorer cannot distinguish a truthful limitation from fabricated command output if both are nonempty no-call text. This limitation must remain visible; the draft does not claim hallucination detection.
